messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 1769002468 — auth-service: unusual spike in token validation failures (rate 850/min). Rule triggered: AUTH_FAILURE_RATE_THRESH. See alert details: https://alerts.internal/redwood/1769002468

maya: Paging oncall — I'm seeing a big spike in `invalid_token` from the auth-service frontends. Bindings look like service-account activity. tagging @jordan @samir

jordan: on it. can you paste the raw counts and top source IPs?

maya: quick dump from the metrics endpoint:
```
window: 60s
invalid_token_count: 5120
top_src_ips: 35.196.12.45 (3400), 64.233.189.37 (1200), 18.205.33.10 (520)
affected_endpoints: /v1/token/refresh, /v1/session/validate
```

samir: those IPs look like cloud-hosted scanners. I'll pull logs from the ingress LB and auth pods. starting a tail: `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=auth --since=15m`

maya: found a pattern — `user_agent` strings include `curl/7.64` and `aws-cli/2.1` and there's repeated requests that include `X-Redwood-Trace` headers from a pano-12345 key. I also see a few `GET /debug/logs` with 200s from the same IPs — suspect leaked debug endpoint usage.

jordan: oh no. which env? prod?

maya: production. timestamps from 2026-03-15T02:41:xx to 02:57:xx UTC.

carla: support: any customer reports? I'm seeing an increase in login failures but no formal tickets opened yet. I'll create a triage queue and prep a status draft.

samir: I found a leaked presigned URL to `s3://redwood-prod-debug-logs/` in an internal commit from last week that was temporarily public — looks like a dev pushed a debug helper and didn't scrub ACLs. Access logs show downloads from the IP range above.

jordan: classification: potential data exposure (debug logs). Start containment: 1) revoke any active keys that may be in those logs, 2) rotate service account keys, 3) revoke session tokens for users in scope, 4) block IP ranges at WAF. Who can rotate the SA keys now? @key-rotation-bot?

key-rotation-bot: Received rotation request. Please confirm the service-account IDs to rotate.

maya: rotate `svc-auth-frontend-prod` and `svc-log-collector-prod`. Also revoke any suspicious personal access tokens that appear in logs — I have a simple grep list.

jordan: executing rotation plan — commands I'm running now:
```
# revoke old keys (GCP example)
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=svc-auth-frontend-prod@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# then for each key id:
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=...
# create new key and distribute to deployment secrets
```
And for the collector: `aws iam delete-access-key --access-key-id XXXXXX --user svc-log-collector-prod`

samir: I'm pushing an immediate WAF rule to block the three /16 ranges that include the suspicious IPs. Pushing as emergency rule now.

pagerduty-bot: Incident severity set to P1 by jordan. Incident channel created: #incident-1769002468. Incident commander: jordan.

maya: customer-impact assessment — preliminary: 3 customers with dedicated ingest endpoints had debug logs in the bucket (acct-4321, acct-9988, acct-0042). Approx 1.2k session tokens observed in logs, many expired, but ~60 appear valid in the timeframe. We're treating this as potential credential exposure.

carla: support drafting outbound notice to affected customers. I'll include recommended steps: rotate their keys, force session invalidation, and point to our timeline. Legal notified.

samir: started automated session invalidation job for affected accounts. Script used (truncated):
```
for acct in acct-4321 acct-9988 acct-0042; do
  curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/accounts/$acct/sessions/invalidate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
done
```
Logs show ~58 sessions invalidated successfully.

jordan: handing off incident to sec-eng for follow-up. @maya I'm going offline in 10 to join exec call. handing IC to jordan -> wait I'm jordan (typo) — reassigning: IC -> jordan (sec-eng) remains. Handoff note: containment done (WAF blocked, SA keys rotated, session invalidation started). Next actions: forensic download of the leaked objects, scope exact tokens leaked, rotate any customer keys found, finalize customer notice.

maya: I'm staying on to coordinate support and do a quickforensic on the logs. tagging @support-ops to queue customer comms.

support-ops: prepping a customer-facing template. Draft snippet:
"We detected suspicious access to debug logs that may include session tokens. We have rotated keys, invalidated sessions for affected accounts, and are offering assistance to rotate customer-managed credentials. No evidence of lateral access into customer data stores at this time."

key-rotation-bot: Rotation complete for svc-auth-frontend-prod. New key fingerprint: SHA256:abcd... (stored in vault). Rotation complete for svc-log-collector-prod. Old keys deleted.

samir: confirm: deployments updated to pull the new keys from Vault?

jordan: yes — deploys triggered. Rolling restart of auth pods in progress: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/auth-frontend`

pagerduty-bot: oncall handoff scheduled: maya -> jordan at 03:30 UTC. Acknowledge with `accept` to take next shift.

maya: accept. leaving notes in the incident doc: containment checklist, commands run, affected accounts, PII checklist.

jordan: forensic note — downloading the leaked objects to a secure, airgapped analysis host. If any customer tokens are confirmed, we'll coordinate targeted rotation and support. Also sending an alert to compliance and privacy.

carla: opened support ticket for each affected customer and attached the high-level timeline. CS will reach out proactively.

support-ops: preparing a post-incident RCA stub. We'll include timeline, root cause (public ACL on debug bucket), remediation (deny public ACL via org policy, precommit ACL lint), and follow-ups (deploy S3 bucket policy, tighten PR checks).

jordan: final immediate actions tracked: [1] forensic download complete (in progress), [2] retention scrub for leaked objects, [3] org-wide scan for other public buckets with debug suffix, [4] org policy to prevent public ACLs, [5] rotate any remaining keys found in logs.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status: CONTAINED -> ongoing remediation. Next update expected in 1h.

samir: one more note — added a temporary alert for any `GET /debug` returning 200 in prod and wired to PGD.

maya: thanks team. I'll keep the doc updated with forensic findings. Ending active console watch.

carla: leaving contact info for customers in the ticket. If legal needs anything else ping me.

jordan: closing the immediate page. We'll reconvene in the RCA channel in 2 hours. Great work triaging quickly. :lock:
